tasks.title: Make evidence revocation and restoration safe and replay-consistent
tasks.description: In orchestrator/creator_dna/store.py, separate creator rejection from attribution revocation. Today revoke_attribution() and reject_evidence() both write evidence_review/reject, _apply() treats every action other than reject as a restore, and restore_evidence() can make evidence from a withdrawn attribution eligible again (also after replay); a revocation of already creator-rejected evidence is not recorded at all. Fix: independent creator_rejected and attribution_revoked state with rejected kept as a read-only compatibility property; a distinct attribution_revoked event (decision ID and reason, schema v4); strict evidence_review actions (reject, restore only); restore clears only creator rejection and is refused for revoked or flagged possible-legacy-revoked evidence; revocation is recorded even for creator-rejected evidence and is idempotent per decision. Legacy v1-v3 logs replay with their original semantics; a note-prefix heuristic may only set read-only warning flags. Synthetic regression tests and a documentation update. No change to speaker_attribution/ or any cross-package test; no real footage.
acceptance_criteria: Creator rejection and attribution revocation are independent state; EvidenceItem.rejected stays a read-only property true for either, and existing readers of rejected and review_note are unchanged
Revocation is written as a distinct attribution_revoked event with decision ID and reason (schema v4); evidence_review accepts only reject and restore and any other action fails replay
restore_evidence clears only creator rejection, never undoes a current revocation, and is refused for revoked evidence and for evidence flagged as a possible legacy revocation
revoke_attribution records a revocation for creator-rejected evidence; repeated revoke_attribution/sync_revocations for the same decision emit no new events
Legacy v1-v3 logs replay with original semantics; ambiguous historical rejects are only flagged (read-only warnings), never migrated or reinterpreted
Exports keep rejected_by_creator creator-specific and expose attribution revocation, decision ID and reason separately

Synthetic regression tests cover revoke then restore, creator reject then revoke, unknown actions, reload/replay equivalence, repeated synchronization and legacy replay/reporting; test_speaker_attribution.py passes unmodified
CREATOR_DNA.md documents the event model, legacy handling and restore rules; the full suite passes with python -B -I
